title: Regular sequences and short exact sequences
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $0\to M_1\xrightarrow{\alpha}M_2\xrightarrow{\beta}M_3\to0$ a short exact sequence of $R$-modules and $f_1,\dots,f_r\in R$. For $0\le i\le r$ write $I_i=(f_1,\dots,f_i)\subset R$. (a) Suppose that for every $i=1,\dots,r$ the element $f_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M_1/I_{i-1}M_1$ and on $M_3/I_{i-1}M_3$ (condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $M_1$ and for $M_3$). Then for every $i=1,\dots,r$ the element $f_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M_2/I_{i-1}M_2$, and for every $0\le i\le r$ the sequence $0\to M_1/I_iM_1\to M_2/I_iM_2\to M_3/I_iM_3\to0$ induced by $\alpha,\beta$ is exact. (b) Consequently, if $f_1,\dots,f_r$ is an $M_1$-regular sequence and an $M_3$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], then it is an $M_2$-regular sequence.

proof.text: Obtain all quotient short exact rows by the snake-lemma consequence [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] already proved in Mathlib as RingTheory.Sequence.map_first_exact_on_four_term_right_exact_of_isSMulRegular_last. Apply it to the four maps 0 -> M1 -> M2 -> M3, with rs weakly regular on M3: exactness of zero followed by a is injectivity of a (Submodule.mapQ_zero and LinearMap.exact_zero_iff_injective). Apply it again to M1 -> M2 -> M3 -> PUnit, where the last map is zero, surjective, and every list is weakly regular on PUnit: this gives exactness of a followed by b. Surjectivity of b follows by lifting a quotient representative first to M3 and then along beta. These applications reuse the quotient induction in Mathlib instead of explicitly constructing a SnakeInput.

proof.text: Translate the hypotheses into IsWeaklyRegular on M1 and M3 [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] using isWeaklyRegular_iff_Fin and isSMulRegular_iff_right_eq_zero_of_smul. Weak regularity of f on M3 restricts to every prefix f.take n by isWeaklyRegular_append_iff and List.take_append_drop. Step 2 therefore gives all the requested prefix rows, including the empty and full prefixes. For i < length f apply Mathlib isSMulRegular_of_range_eq_ker to the row modulo the preceding prefix, using injectivity of a, exactness (range a = ker b), and the given scalar regularity on both outer quotient modules. This gives the middle nonzerodivisor assertion and completes part (a).

proof.text: For part (b), IsRegular on the outer terms [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] supplies the hypotheses of part (a), giving IsWeaklyRegular on M2. To prove the nonvanishing condition, suppose top = Ideal.ofList f smul top on M2. Apply Submodule.map beta to this equality, rewrite Submodule.map_smul'' and Submodule.map_top, and use surjectivity of beta (range beta = top). The resulting equality top = Ideal.ofList f smul top on M3 contradicts its IsRegular.top_ne_smul. Hence f is regular on M2.

lean.statement: theorem isRegular_of_shortExact (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M₁ : Type v₁) (M₂ : Type v₂) (M₃ : Type v₃) [AddCommGroup M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₁] [Module R M₂] [Module R M₃] (α : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (β : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃) (hα : Function.Injective α) (hβ : Function.Surjective β) (hex : Function.Exact α β) (f : List R) : (((∀ (i : Fin f.length) (x : M₁ ⧸ ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₁))), f.get i • x = 0 → x = 0) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin f.length) (x : M₃ ⧸ ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₃))), f.get i • x = 0 → x = 0) → (∀ (i : Fin f.length) (x : M₂ ⧸ ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₂))), f.get i • x = 0 → x = 0) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin (f.length + 1)), ∃ (a : M₁ ⧸ ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₁)) →ₗ[R] M₂ ⧸ ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₂))) (b : M₂ ⧸ ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₂)) →ₗ[R] M₃ ⧸ ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₃))), Function.Exact a b ∧ Function.Injective a ∧ Function.Surjective b ∧ (∀ x : M₁, a (((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₁)).mkQ x) = ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₂)).mkQ (α x))) ∧ (∀ x : M₂, b (((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1)) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₂)).mkQ x) = ((Ideal.ofList (f.take i.1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M₃)).mkQ (β x)))) ∧ ((IsRegular M₁ f ∧ IsRegular M₃ f) → IsRegular M₂ f)
